tv: a fuzzy finder with channels for everything

The problem it solves

All day I look for things: a file, a git branch, a test, a command from my history, a recipe. Over the years I had collected a drawer full of one-off fzf scripts, each with its own keys, its own look and its own quirks, and none with a preview.

The general idea

television (the command is tv) is a fuzzy finder with one big idea: channels. A channel is a small TOML file that says where the candidates come from, how to preview the selected one and what to do with it. Files, git branches, shell history, running processes: each is a channel, and you can write your own in a few lines. Every channel looks and behaves the same.

Examples

This channel of mine lists test files and individual test functions, and runs the chosen one with uv:

[metadata]
name = "pytest"
description = "Select a test file or function to run with pytest"

[source]
command = "{ find test tests -name '*.py' -not -path '*/.*' -type f 2>/dev/null; grep -rn '^\\s*def test_' test tests 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's|:[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*def (test_[^( ]+).*|::\\1|'; } | awk 'NF'"
no_sort = true

[actions.execute]
description = "Run"
command = "uv run pytest -s '{}'"
mode = "execute"

The source command prints the candidates, one per line. An actions block says what happens on the selected entry, and {} stands for it. That is the whole mechanism.

Tips from my setup

  • The channels I use most: files (the default) and dirs, git-branch, git-log and git-repos, and a filtered version of my zsh history. The ones I wrote myself are just-recipes, pytest and python-modules.
  • A channel for just recipes. It collects the recipes of the local and the global Justfile, shows just -s name as the preview (so I read a recipe before running it) and binds a function key to run the selection: 
    [preview]
command = "just -s '{split:\t:1}'"

[keybindings]
f5 = "actions:execute-recipe"
  • Shell integration. With it, Ctrl-T opens the channel that fits what I am typing. The mapping from commands to channels is a few lines in the config, for example: 
    [shell_integration.channel_triggers]
"git-branch" = ["git checkout", "git switch"]
"dirs" = ["cd", "ls"]
"files" = ["cat", "nvim"]
  • A rule of thumb. When I notice that I look for the same kind of thing twice, I write a channel. A new channel is a file, not a project.
